sn7.13:1.2: _Vātehābādhika_ is a syntactic compound, “afflicted by winds” (_vātehi_). It is one of the illnesses noted at [an10.60:7.4](). In Ayurveda, diseases of the winds may have many causes, chief among them faulty digestion.
sn7.13:1.3: In [dn16:5.4.5]() Upavāna was said to have been the Buddha’s carer for a long time. At [dn29:41.1]() he is fanning the Buddha. At [an5.166](), Ānanda goes to Upavāṇa for support when he feels he has disappointed the Buddha. The events of this discourse are recalled by him in his verses at [thag2.33]().
sn7.13:1.5: Typically ghee or other oil is recommended rather than hot water.
